text: Code reviews are a vital part of modern software development. When a developer finishes writing a piece of code, another team member carefully examines it before it is merged into the main project. This process is excellent for catching bugs early, as a fresh pair of eyes can often spot mistakes that the original author missed. Fixing a small issue at this stage is much cheaper than dealing with a major problem later. However, reviews are not just about finding errors. They also promote knowledge sharing, allowing team members to learn new techniques and understand different parts of the codebase. Ultimately, a consistent review culture strengthens overall team quality, leading to more reliable software and more confident developers.
